title: Face Cream Jar Shoulder-Neck Box: Lid Fit and Jar Removal
seoTitle: Face Cream Shoulder-Neck Box Fit Guide | MTT
summary: Plan a cream jar shoulder-neck gift box around the lid, raised neck, insert and customer removal.
intro: We start a face cream presentation box by placing the filled jar in the proposed insert and lifting it back out. A shoulder-neck box adds another decision: its separate lid must fit over the raised inner neck without trapping the jar or making the box difficult to open. We would review the closed sample, jar access and outer shipping pack together before releasing the design.
cta: Send the filled jar and lid dimensions, weight, artwork, quantity per design and shipping destination. MTT can review the structure and sample brief for orders from 1,000 boxes per design.
sections: Understand the three-part construction

A shoulder-neck structure has a base, an inner neck rising above it, and a separate lid that locates around the neck. The visible shoulder band and depth of lid overlap are appearance decisions as well as fit decisions. Ask the converter to show the neck height, lid depth, board and wrap on a dimensioned drawing; a photograph alone does not establish these measurements.

The face cream jar shoulder-neck box is a design reference with a centred jar position. Its image is not a measured sample, a customer case or evidence of a passed shipping test.
Measure the whole jar, then draw the removal path

Measure the maximum jar diameter including the closed lid, overall height, base shape and filled weight. Identify any label seam or decorated face that should not rub. Ask the container supplier for its specified dimensional range; a single representative jar cannot establish the full production tolerance.

Now place the jar in the proposed insert. Can a finger reach the jar body, or does the raised neck obstruct it? An insert that fits tightly around the lid can force the recipient to grip or twist the product closure. Compare a finger recess, a support arrangement that exposes a safe grip area, or another agreed removal method on a physical sample.
Compare the lid in three conditions

Checks for a finished face cream box sample
ConditionQuestionRecord
Empty shellDoes the lid seat and lift smoothly on the wrapped neck?Sample and drawing revision
Insert installedDoes the insert remain seated and clear the lid?Insert material and position
Filled jar and card installedCan the lid close without touching the jar or accessory?Jar revision, clearance observations and photos
Jar removedCan the jar be lifted without disturbing the insert?Grip method and contact marks

Agree how much opening resistance and visible lid alignment are acceptable for the project. There is no universal overlap or clearance in this guide: finished board, wrap, assembly variation and the actual jar all matter.
Work through a change before approving tooling

Illustrative example: a brand selects a jar by nominal capacity and approves an attractive rendering. The final jar lid is wider than the initial reference, and the neck leaves little room for fingers. We would update the product envelope and review both the opening and the removal path on a revised sample. The example is hypothetical; it is not an MTT order or measured defect.

Check the largest permitted jar against the smallest permitted opening using the agreed component specifications. If the range is unknown, keep the insert drawing provisional rather than presenting a guessed allowance as a production tolerance. See the dimension measurement guide.
Separate presentation from delivery protection

The presentation insert locates the jar for opening; it does not by itself establish that a filled glass jar is protected in a courier network. Define whether the sets go to a store, a fulfilment centre or directly to customers, and ask who supplies the outer carton and cushioning. ISTA recommends identifying the actual distribution environment and agreeing product damage criteria before selecting an appropriate test.[1]

Request an itemised quotation for shell, insert, print and foil, tooling, sample and shipping. State quantities and artwork versions separately; MTT projects begin at 1,000 boxes per design.
Sources
1. ISTA: guidelines for selecting and using packaged-product tests, accessed 16 November 2026.

imageAlt: Perfume gift bag concept with ribbon handles for discussing loaded carrying
title: Perfume Gift Bag Handles: Check the Loaded Box, Anchors and Base
seoTitle: Perfume Gift Bag Handle & Base Checks | MTT
summary: Specify a matching perfume gift bag around the finished box, carrying load, handle attachment and sample review.
intro: We begin a matching perfume bag with the complete filled gift box, not just the bottle. The box must slide into the bag, sit on its base and leave the customer enough room to hold the handles. We would review the handle attachment, top reinforcement and bottom construction as a complete loaded sample before agreeing a project-specific carrying check.
cta: Send the finished box dimensions, full carrying weight, bag orientation, handle preference, quantity per design and destination. MTT can review the bag brief for orders from 1,000 pieces per design.
sections: Measure the finished set, including accessories

List the external box length, width and height after wrapping and assembly. Identify the orientation in which it enters the bag and include any ribbon, card, tissue or second item. Record the complete intended carrying weight with the filled bottle and primary packaging. A nominal perfume volume is not a bag load or an external box size.

The accompanying image is a handle concept, not a load-tested sample. Compare the box and bag together using the matching perfume box and bag guide; this article concentrates on carrying loads and the sample acceptance record.
Follow the load from hand to base

When a customer lifts the set, the handle transfers the load through its attachment into the bag body and bottom. Identify the handle material, length, attachment method, top fold or reinforcement, side seams and base construction. A paper specification alone cannot describe the whole finished assembly. Industry paper-bag guidance discusses handle attachment and reinforcement as parts of bag construction.[1]

Request a finished sample with the actual handle and bottom components. Check where knots, tabs or reinforcement sit relative to the box, and whether the filled box rests evenly on the base. If a knot protrudes into the bag, review whether it catches or marks the wrapped box during insertion.
Compare two handle routes on the finished bag

Handle and base questions before sample approval
PartAsk the converterCheck with the actual set
Cord or ribbon handlesHow are they attached and reinforced?Grip comfort, attachment and contact with box
Paper handlesWhat is the handle and reinforcement construction?Folding, grip and attachment under the agreed load
Top and side seamsWhich surfaces are folded or bonded?Any separation, distortion or box snagging
BaseIs an insert or reinforcement included?Box sits flat; base remains supported during handling

These are questions for comparison, not a statement that every handle type suits the same weight or that a specific construction has passed a test.
Write a carrying check both sides can repeat

Before examining samples, agree the representative load, bag orientation, conditioning, lifting and carrying method, number of repetitions, and acceptable changes to the handles, seams and base. Photograph and identify the sample before and after the agreed handling. If a formal standard is required, agree its exact edition and method with the testing provider; an informal lift is screening, not a certified load rating.

Illustrative example: a brand changes from one perfume box to a box plus a refill. The bag artwork stays the same, but the combined size and carrying weight change. Recheck insertion, the loaded base and the agreed handle evaluation on the new complete set. This is a hypothetical procurement scenario, not an MTT test result.
Keep the quote comparable

Specify finished bag width, gusset and height, the box insertion orientation, intended load, paper and finish, handle and reinforcement, and quantities per artwork. Ask for the box, bag, sample, tooling and freight as separate lines. Confirm who supplies and packs the contents and whether the bag is used for retail carrying or forms part of a separate shipping arrangement. Review custom paper bag options and prepare a sample brief for at least 1,000 pieces per design.
Sources
1. CEPI Eurokraft and EUROSAC: industry guidelines for quality paper bags, accessed 16 November 2026.
